suggestions: Meaning change at L19: "Two cases show the grid is a business lever, not a derived value" credits both cases as proof. In the original only office drop-in is the proof; the on-site case is about packing scarce room time.

Meaning change at L63: "The second is the stronger" turns the original's "more interesting" into a ranking of the options the original did not make. It also says edge-based ranking was deprecated for "reordering", but the original says it was deprecated for outside-in filling.
L52 heading "Edge-awareness is wrong for sparse days, not wrong." is garbled. It means "not wrong in general".

Dropped content not covered by assertions: "or something already under design review" (6.5), the 6.4 framing sentence that today's per-type grid may not be the right long-term model (the heading still implies it), and the note that edge-based ranking was "rejected on purpose, not left unfinished".
eval_feedback.overall: 20/20 facts retained. It is the shortest output, and the compression caused two small meaning shifts: the business-lever proof is credited to both cases (L19), and grid-follows-the-gap is called "stronger" with a reframed deprecation cause (L63).
